name: The Amazon (Puerto Maldonado)
tagline: Peru's gateway to the Amazon, one of the most biodiverse regions on Earth, reached by boat deep into the rainforest.
highlight: Watching dozens of macaws descend on a riverbank clay lick at dawn, a chaotic wash of red, blue and green against the mud.
shortDescription: Peru's easiest gateway into the Amazon rainforest, home to giant river otters, macaw clay licks and some of the most biodiverse jungle on Earth.
metaDescription: An Amazon Peru travel guide: Lake Sandoval, Tambopata, wildlife spotting, food and how to plan a rainforest lodge visit from Puerto Maldonado.
knownFor: The Amazon rainforest, giant river otters, macaw clay licks

intro: Puerto Maldonado is Peru's easiest gateway into the Amazon, a small jungle town at the meeting point of the Madre de Dios and Tambopata rivers, and the starting point for lodge stays deep in the rainforest.

The surrounding region is one of the most biodiverse places on Earth, part of the Tambopata National Reserve, home to giant river otters, hundreds of bird species and macaw clay licks found in only a handful of places worldwide.
Most visitors arrive on an all-inclusive multi-night lodge package, travelling upriver by boat to a remote setting with no road access, guided daily wildlife excursions built into the stay.

whyVisit.intro: The Amazon's case rests on extraordinary biodiversity, reached more easily here than almost anywhere else in South America.

points.title: It's one of the most biodiverse regions on Earth
points.text: Part of the Tambopata National Reserve, home to extraordinary concentrations of species.

points.title: Giant river otters are a real, reliable sighting
points.text: Lake Sandoval holds a resident family, among the most accessible sightings anywhere.

points.title: Macaw clay licks are found in only a few places worldwide
points.text: Dozens of macaws and parrots gathering at riverbank clay deposits each morning.

points.title: It's more accessible than other Amazon gateways
points.text: A short flight from Cusco puts you deep in the rainforest within hours.

points.title: Lodge stays include expert local guiding
points.text: Naturalist guides bring real expertise most independent travellers couldn't match alone.

attractionsIntro: The region's essential sights combine extraordinary wildlife with an immersive rainforest setting reached only by river.

attractions.name: Lake Sandoval

image.alt: Lake Sandoval in the Peruvian Amazon

attractions.text: A stunning oxbow lake reached by a jungle trail and canoe, home to giant river otters, caimans and abundant birdlife.
attractions.tip: The walk in takes about an hour each way — wear sturdy, waterproof footwear.

attractions.name: Giant river otters

image.alt: A giant river otter at Lake Sandoval

attractions.text: One of the region's star sightings, a family of endangered giant otters resident on Lake Sandoval.
attractions.tip: Early morning canoe trips offer the best chance of spotting the otters actively fishing.

attractions.name: Caimans of Lake Sandoval

image.alt: A caiman resting at Lake Sandoval

attractions.text: A common sighting on night canoe trips, black caimans resting along the lake's quieter shores.
attractions.tip: A spotlight night excursion offers the best chance of a close caiman sighting.

attractions.name: Macaw clay licks

image.file: File:Parrots at a clay lick -Tambopata National Reserve, Peru-8c.jpg
image.alt: Macaws gathering at a clay lick in Tambopata

attractions.text: One of the Amazon's great wildlife spectacles, dozens of macaws and parrots gathering at riverbank clay deposits each dawn.
attractions.tip: Requires an early start, but the clay lick's chaotic colour and noise is unforgettable.

attractions.name: Tambopata National Reserve

image.file: File:Tree frog in bamboo forest, Tambopata National Reserve, Peru.jpg

attractions.text: A protected reserve of extraordinary biodiversity, home to jaguars, tapirs and hundreds of bird species, even if many are elusive.
attractions.tip: Manage expectations on big mammal sightings — insects, birds and reptiles are far more reliably seen.

attractions.name: The Amazon rainforest canopy

image.alt: The dense rainforest canopy near Puerto Maldonado

attractions.text: A dense, layered ecosystem best appreciated from a canopy tower or elevated walkway at many jungle lodges.
attractions.tip: Dawn and dusk from a canopy platform offer the most active wildlife viewing.

attractions.name: Puerto Maldonado

image.alt: An aerial view of Puerto Maldonado at the edge of the Amazon

attractions.text: A small, functional jungle town at the confluence of two rivers, the practical gateway for onward lodge travel.
attractions.tip: Most visitors pass through quickly, spending only a night here before or after a lodge stay.

thingsToDoIntro: The Amazon rewards patience, with the best wildlife sightings coming from guided excursions at dawn and dusk.

thingsToDo.title: Spot giant river otters at Lake Sandoval

image.alt: Watching giant river otters at Lake Sandoval

thingsToDo.text: A thrilling early-morning canoe trip, watching one of the Amazon's most endangered mammals in its natural habitat.
thingsToDo.tip: Bring a zoom lens or binoculars — otters keep a respectful distance from canoes.

thingsToDo.title: Watch macaws at a clay lick

image.file: File:Parrots at a clay lick -Tambopata National Reserve, Peru-8d.jpg
image.alt: Macaws at a riverside clay lick

thingsToDo.text: An unforgettable dawn spectacle, dozens of macaws descending in a wash of colour to eat mineral-rich clay.
thingsToDo.tip: Arrive before sunrise and stay quiet — sudden noise can scare the birds away.

thingsToDo.title: Search for caimans by night

image.alt: Spotting caimans at night in the Amazon

thingsToDo.text: An atmospheric excursion, gliding silently by canoe as a guide's spotlight picks out caiman eyes along the shore.
thingsToDo.tip: Dress warmly — jungle nights on the water are cooler than daytime temperatures suggest.

thingsToDo.title: Explore Tambopata's rainforest trails

image.file: File:Owl Butterfly (Caligo) at night in Tambopata National Reserve, Peru.jpg
image.alt: Wildlife spotted on a night walk in Tambopata

thingsToDo.text: An eye-opening guided night walk, revealing an entirely different set of species active after dark.
thingsToDo.tip: A good guide can spot camouflaged insects and frogs that are otherwise invisible.

thingsToDo.title: Spot mealy parrots along the river

image.alt: A mealy parrot in the Peruvian Amazon

thingsToDo.text: A rewarding, easy sighting for birdwatchers, common along the Tambopata River's forested banks.
thingsToDo.tip: Bring binoculars — many bird sightings here are at a distance in the canopy.

thingsToDo.title: Watch birds dry their feathers at Lake Sandoval

image.alt: Birds drying their feathers at Lake Sandoval

thingsToDo.text: A peaceful sight, cormorants and other water birds spreading their wings to dry along the lake's edge.
thingsToDo.tip: A quiet moment of canoe stillness improves the chances of a close, unhurried view.

foodIntro: Amazonian food differs from the rest of Peru, built around river fish, tropical fruit and jungle staples.

foods.name: Juanes
foods.text: A classic Amazonian dish, rice and chicken seasoned and wrapped in bijao leaves, then steamed.

foods.name: Fresh river fish
foods.text: A highlight of any Amazon visit, species like paiche or dorado grilled simply and served fresh.
foods.whereToTry: Jungle lodges and restaurants throughout Puerto Maldonado.

foods.name: Tropical Amazonian fruit
foods.text: A real treat, exotic fruits like camu camu and aguaje rarely found outside the region.
foods.whereToTry: Markets and lodges throughout the area.

foods.name: Lomo saltado

foods.text: A familiar comfort option, found even this deep in the jungle at most lodges and restaurants.

foods.name: Pisco sour

image.alt: A pisco sour, Peru's national cocktail

foods.text: A fitting way to unwind after a day of wildlife spotting, served at most jungle lodges.

bestTime.headline: June to October for the dry season, offering the easiest wildlife spotting
bestTime.summary: The Amazon's own separate dry season differs from the Andean highlands, with lower water levels concentrating wildlife near rivers.

seasons.text: The easiest wildlife spotting, with lower water levels concentrating animals near rivers and clay licks.
Fewer crowds with still-decent wildlife spotting conditions.
Lush and dramatic, with higher water levels making some trails inaccessible, though birdlife remains excellent.

bestTime.avoid: Expecting guaranteed big-mammal sightings in any season — most Amazon wildlife is elusive, and birds, insects and reptiles are the more reliable highlights.

tipsIntro: Practical notes that make an Amazon lodge visit noticeably smoother.
tips: Book a multi-night lodge package rather than a single day trip — wildlife sightings improve significantly with more time.
Pack lightweight, quick-dry clothing in neutral colours, plus a rain jacket regardless of season.
Bring strong insect repellent and consider anti-malarial medication after consulting a doctor.
Pack binoculars — most wildlife sightings here are at a distance.
Manage expectations on jaguar or big-cat sightings, which are rare even for experienced guides.
Confirm your lodge's cancellation policy given the real possibility of river-level or weather delays.

faq.q: How many days do you need in the Amazon?
faq.a: Three to four days allows for a proper lodge stay with multiple wildlife excursions, improving your odds significantly over a rushed single day.

faq.q: Is Puerto Maldonado a good Amazon gateway?
faq.a: Yes, one of the most accessible, reachable by a short flight from Cusco directly into the rainforest.
Likely for birds, insects, caimans and often giant otters, though large mammals like jaguars are rare, elusive sightings even for experienced guides.

faq.q: What is the Amazon near Puerto Maldonado known for?
faq.a: Extraordinary biodiversity, including reliable giant river otter sightings and spectacular macaw clay licks found in only a few places worldwide.

faq.q: Do you need vaccinations for the Amazon?
faq.a: Consult a travel doctor ahead of your trip — yellow fever vaccination and malaria precautions are commonly recommended for this region.

faq.q: Can you combine the Amazon with Machu Picchu in one trip?
faq.a: Yes — Puerto Maldonado connects easily to Cusco by short flight, making it a natural addition to a wider Peru itinerary.
